text: ok so this looks right, but i need your help just understanding where would be the right place to connect. so, lets look here [Image #2] i have 3 lanes on one side, and 1 on the other. i put A B C on the road. if i want to bring in a 0 on one side and 2 on the other so that i merge into a 3x3 lane where would i click to merge, a b or c? or none of them
resolution: Answered the A/B/C question and closed the gap it exposed (commit 7254c0857). Answer: A and B were the only connect points before this commit (endpoint snap); C was the RIGHT place but mid-stroke connections didn't exist. Now they do: clicking within 1.5 cells of a road's centerline snaps onto the wire, and committing a stroke that ENDS there splits the underlying road at that point — the split seam stays one continuous road via the parallel-axes rule (tested: a split road never boxes at its own seam). Companion capability the merge needs: the rail's lane steppers now LIVE-edit the SELECTED road (restamp on every change, 'editing Road N' badge) instead of only shaping the next draft. The user's exact merge recipe: click C to split, draw the 2-lane one-way into C flowing toward the direction it feeds, select the downstream half (toward A for the northbound side), bump its opposing-lane count 1→3. 16/16 planner cases green, cart bundles clean, TSX-only (hot-reloads).
